Permissions required: 'view-d-room' and, if applicable, 'view-outside-room'. The response includes user details such as id, username, email, type, roles, status, and more. Pagination is supported with 'offset' and 'count' parameters.

output.summary: Create a new public channel.
output.description: Creates a new public channel in Rocket.Chat. You can specify the channel name and optionally include a list of users to add to the channel upon creation. Additional options such as read-only status, custom fields, and other channel settings can also be set. The authenticated user must have the appropriate permissions to create channels.

output.summary: Add all users to a public channel.
output.description: Adds all users in the workspace to a public channel. Requires the 'add-all-to-room' permission. You can optionally add only active users by setting the 'activeUsersOnly' parameter to true. The maximum number of users that can be added at once depends on your workspace's REST API settings (see Administration > Settings > General > REST API > User Limit for Adding All Users to Channel).

output.summary: Assign the leader role to a channel member.
output.description: Assigns the role of 'leader' to a specified user in a channel. The user must already be a member of the channel. Requires the 'set-leader' permission. You must provide both the channel's roomId and the userId of the member to be promoted. If the user is already a leader, the request will fail with an appropriate error. See Rocket.Chat documentation for more about room roles.

output.summary: Add a moderator to a channel.
output.description: Assigns the moderator role to a user in a specified channel. The user must be a member of the channel, and the requester must have appropriate permissions to manage roles in the channel. This endpoint requires the channel ID or name and the username of the user to be promoted.

output.summary: Add an owner to a channel.
output.description: Assigns the owner role to a user in a specified channel. The user must be a member of the channel, and the requester must have appropriate permissions to manage channel roles. This endpoint is useful for delegating channel management responsibilities to additional users.

output.summary: Retrieve messages from a public channel as an anonymous user.
output.description: Allows anonymous (not logged-in) users to read messages from a public channel if the server is configured to permit anonymous read access. This endpoint is useful for integrations or public widgets where users do not have Rocket.Chat accounts. Server settings must explicitly allow anonymous reading for this endpoint to function.

output.summary: Archive a public channel.
output.description: Archives a public channel, making it read-only and removing it from the channel list. Only users with the necessary permissions can archive a channel. The request typically requires the channel's unique identifier or name in the payload. Once archived, no new messages can be sent in the channel until it is unarchived.

output.summary: Close a public channel.
output.description: Closes a public channel, making it inaccessible to users until it is reopened. This endpoint requires the channel ID or name and appropriate permissions. Once closed, the channel will no longer appear in the list of open channels for its members, but it is not deleted and can be reopened later if needed.

output.summary: Get counters and statistics for a channel.
output.description: Retrieves various counters for a channel, such as whether the user has joined, the number of members, and the count of unread messages for the specified user. Requires the 'view-room-administration' permission. You can specify the channel by room ID or name, and optionally provide a user ID to get counters for a different user.

output.summary: Delete a public channel.
output.description: Deletes an existing public channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier or name. Only users with the appropriate permissions can delete channels. This action is irreversible and will remove all messages and files associated with the channel.

output.summary: List files shared in a public channel.
output.description: Retrieves a list of files that have been uploaded to a specified public channel. This endpoint requires the channel ID as a parameter and returns metadata about each file, such as the file name, uploader, and upload date. Authentication is required, and the user must have permission to view the channel. Pagination parameters may be supported to limit the number of results returned.

output.summary: Retrieve the message history of a public channel.
output.description: Fetches the messages from a specified public channel. This endpoint supports pagination and optional parameters such as date ranges, message count, and inclusion of additional message metadata. Authentication is required, and the user must have permission to view the channel. Useful for loading chat history, searching messages, or exporting channel conversations.

output.summary: Get information about a public channel.
output.description: Retrieves information about a public channel in Rocket.Chat. You can provide either the channel's roomId or roomName as a query parameter. The response includes details such as the channel's name, topic, members, and other metadata. This endpoint is useful for obtaining channel details for display or management purposes. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Invite a user to a public channel.
output.description: Invites a user to a public channel by specifying the channel ID and the user ID. The user will be added to the channel if they are not already a member. Requires appropriate permissions to invite users to the channel.

output.summary: Join a user to a public channel.
output.description: Allows an authenticated user to join a public channel by specifying the channel's name or ID. The user must not already be a member of the channel. This endpoint requires authentication and only works for public channels (not private groups).

output.summary: Remove a user from a public channel.
output.description: Removes a specified user from a public channel. The request typically requires the channel ID and the user ID of the member to be removed. The authenticated user must have the necessary permissions to perform this action. This endpoint is useful for moderating channel membership and managing user access to public channels.

output.summary: Leave a public channel.
output.description: Removes the authenticated user from a public channel. The user must have the 'leave-c' permission. You must provide the channel's roomId in the request body. If the user is the last owner of the channel, they must assign another owner before leaving. On success, the response includes the updated channel information.

output.summary: List all channels the authenticated user has joined.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all public channels that the authenticated user is a member of. This endpoint returns channel information such as channel IDs, names, and other metadata. Pagination parameters can be used to limit results. Authentication is required.

output.summary: List all public channels in the server.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all public channels in the server that the authenticated user has access to. The response includes channel details such as name, id, and other metadata. Supports pagination and can be filtered using query parameters. Authentication is required.

output.summary: List the members of a public channel.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all users who are members of a specified public channel. You must provide the channel's unique ID or name as a parameter. The response may include pagination fields such as 'count', 'offset', and 'total'. This endpoint is useful for managing or displaying channel membership information. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve messages from a public channel.
output.description: Fetches the messages from a specified public channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier or name as a parameter. The response includes an array of message objects and may support pagination through optional query parameters such as count and offset. Authentication is required to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Get the list of moderators for a channel.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all moderators assigned to a specific channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier (roomId) or name as a parameter. The response includes user information for each moderator. Appropriate permissions are required to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Get a list of online users in a channel.
output.description: Retrieves a list of users who are currently online in a specified public channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier (roomId) as a query parameter. This endpoint is useful for checking which members of a channel are currently active. Requires the user to have permission to view the channel.

output.summary: Open a channel for the calling user.
output.description: Opens a channel that was previously closed or archived for the calling user. This endpoint is useful for restoring access to a channel without creating a new one. The user regains access to the channel and its messages. Requires authentication.

output.summary: Remove the leader role from a user in a public channel.
output.description: Removes the 'leader' role from a specified user in a public channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier (roomId) or name, and the username of the user whose leader role should be removed. The authenticated user must have appropriate permissions to manage roles in the channel. This endpoint is useful for managing channel leadership and permissions dynamically.

output.summary: Remove a moderator from a channel.
output.description: Removes the moderator role from a specified user in a channel. The request requires the channel ID or name and the user ID or username to be provided. The authenticated user must have appropriate permissions to manage roles in the channel. This endpoint is useful for managing channel moderation and access control.

output.summary: Remove an owner from a channel.
output.description: Removes the owner role from a specified user in a channel. The request must include the channel ID or name and the user ID or username to be removed as owner. The user making the request must have appropriate permissions to manage channel roles.

output.summary: Rename a public channel.
output.description: Renames an existing public channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier (roomId) and the new name. Only users with the appropriate permissions (such as channel owners or administrators) can rename a channel. The new name must be unique and comply with channel naming rules. This endpoint is useful for updating channel names to reflect changes in purpose or organization.

output.summary: Get the roles of users in a public channel.
output.description: Retrieves a list of users and their assigned roles (such as owner, moderator, or leader) for a specified public channel. You must provide the channel ID as a parameter. This endpoint is useful for managing permissions and understanding the structure of channel membership. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Set the announcement for a channel.
output.description: Sets or updates the announcement text for a specific channel. Requires the channel's unique identifier (roomId or name) and the new announcement text. The user must have appropriate permissions to modify the channel announcement. This endpoint is useful for sharing important information or updates with all channel members.

output.summary: Set custom fields for a channel.
output.description: Sets or updates custom fields for a specified channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier and a customFields object containing key-value pairs to store as custom metadata for the channel. Authentication and appropriate permissions are required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Set whether a channel is a default channel.
output.description: Set whether the channel is a default channel or not. When a channel is set as default, all new users will automatically join this channel upon account creation. Requires the 'edit-room' permission. You must provide the channel's roomId and a boolean value for 'default' in the request body.

output.summary: Set the description for a channel.
output.description: Sets or updates the description of a channel. You must provide the channel's unique identifier or name and the new description text. The user must have permission to edit the channel's information. This endpoint is useful for updating channel details to provide more context or information to its members.

output.summary: Set a join code for a public channel.
output.description: Sets or updates the join code (password) required to join a public channel. This endpoint allows administrators or users with the appropriate permissions to restrict access to a channel by requiring users to enter a join code before joining. The request must include the channel ID and the desired join code.

output.summary: Set the purpose of a channel.
output.description: Sets or updates the purpose (description) of a channel. You must provide the channel ID or name and the new purpose text. This endpoint requires appropriate permissions to modify the channel's information.

output.summary: Set a channel to read-only or writable.
output.description: Sets a channel to read-only or allows it to be writable again. This endpoint requires the channel ID or name and a boolean value indicating whether the channel should be read-only. Only users with the appropriate permissions can change this setting. When a channel is set to read-only, only authorized users (such as moderators or owners) can send messages in the channel, while others can only view messages.

output.summary: Set the topic for a channel.
output.description: Sets or updates the topic of a specified channel. You must provide the channel ID or name and the new topic text. Requires appropriate permissions to modify the channel's topic.

output.summary: Change the type of a channel between public and private.
output.description: Change the type of a channel (room) between public and private. This endpoint allows you to convert a public channel to private or vice versa by specifying the channel ID and the desired type. Only users with the appropriate permissions can perform this action. The response will include the updated channel information if successful.

output.summary: Unarchive a public channel.
output.description: Unarchives a previously archived public channel, making it active and accessible again. The user must have the necessary permissions to unarchive the channel. Provide the channel ID or name in the request body to specify which channel to unarchive.

output.summary: Retrieve all user mentions in a channel.
output.description: Fetches all messages in a specified channel where users have been mentioned. This endpoint is useful for tracking mentions and notifications within a channel. You will typically need to provide the channel ID or name as a parameter. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve integrations for a channel.
output.description: Retrieves the integrations that are configured for a specific channel. To use this endpoint, the user must have at least one of the following permissions: manage-incoming-integrations, manage-own-incoming-integrations, manage-outgoing-integrations, or manage-own-outgoing-integrations. The response will include only the integrations the user is authorized to view, based on their permissions. You must specify the channel's roomId as a query parameter. Optional parameters such as offset, count, sort, fields, and query can be used to paginate and filter the results.

output.summary: Convert a public channel to a team.
output.description: Converts an existing public channel into a team. You must provide the channel ID or name. Only public channels that are not already teams can be converted. After conversion, the channel will have team features enabled, and its members will become team members. Appropriate permissions are required to perform this action.

output.summary: Save a notification setting for a room.
output.description: Save or update a notification setting for a specific room. This endpoint allows you to configure notification preferences such as desktop, mobile, or email notifications for a room. You must provide the room ID and the notification settings you wish to apply. Only users with appropriate permissions can modify notification settings for a room.

output.summary: List all rooms on the server (admin only)
output.description: Retrieves a list of all rooms in the server, accessible only to users with admin privileges. This endpoint supports filtering, sorting, and pagination through query parameters. It is typically used for administrative purposes such as moderation, auditing, or management of rooms. Proper permissions are required to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Delete messages from a room within a specified time range.
output.description: Cleans up a room by removing messages from the provided time range. You can specify the room, the oldest and latest dates, whether to include pinned messages, whether to delete only files, limit the number of messages, and target specific users. By default, all messages in the range are deleted, but you can fine-tune the operation with additional parameters. Permission required: clean-channel-history. For more details, see the 'Prune messages from a room' section in the Rocket.Chat documentation.

output.summary: Get information about a room.
output.description: Retrieves details about a specific room (channel, group, or direct message) by room ID or name. You must provide either the roomId or roomName as a query parameter. The response includes information such as the room type, name, topic, and other metadata. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve discussions for a room.
output.description: Fetches all discussions related to a specific room. This endpoint returns a list of discussion threads that are associated with the given room, allowing you to view and manage threaded conversations within that room. You may need to provide the room ID as a parameter to filter the discussions accordingly.

output.summary: Get all opened rooms of the authenticated user.
output.description: Retrieves all opened rooms (including all joined public and private channels, and all direct messages) for the authenticated user. You can optionally provide the 'updatedSince' query parameter as an ISO date string to only return rooms that have been updated or removed since the specified date and time. The response includes arrays for updated and removed rooms. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Leave a room or channel.
output.description: Allows the authenticated user to leave a room or channel. The user will no longer receive messages or notifications from the room after leaving. This endpoint requires the room ID or name as a parameter. If the user is not a member of the room, an error will be returned.

output.summary: Delete a room (channel, group, or direct message).
output.description: Deletes a room (channel, private group, or direct message) by its ID. The user must have the appropriate permissions to delete the room. This action is irreversible and will remove all messages and files associated with the room. Use with caution.

output.summary: Mark or unmark a room as favorite for the user.
output.description: Marks or unmarks a room as a favorite for the authenticated user. To use this endpoint, provide the room ID and a boolean flag indicating whether to favorite (true) or unfavorite (false) the room. This helps users organize their room list by highlighting important rooms. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Upload a file to a room.
output.description: Uploads a file to the specified room by its room ID. The file should be sent as multipart/form-data in the request body. Authentication is required. Additional parameters such as a message or description can often be included with the upload. The response will include information about the uploaded file and its message in the room.

output.summary: Upload media files to a room.
output.description: Upload media files (such as images, videos, or documents) to a specific room by room ID. The file and an accompanying message text must be provided as multipart/form-data. The response includes the file ID and its URL. This endpoint replaces the deprecated /rooms.upload/{rid} endpoint.

output.summary: Get media files shared in a room.
output.description: Retrieves a list of media files (such as images, videos, and audio) that have been shared in the specified room. The room is identified by its unique room ID (rid). This endpoint is useful for displaying or managing all media content within a room. Pagination and filtering options may be available depending on the server configuration. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Get rooms available to add to a team using autocomplete.
output.description: Retrieves a list of rooms that are eligible to be added to a team, filtered by an autocomplete search term. This endpoint is typically used to help users quickly find and select rooms when managing team memberships. You may provide a search term to narrow down the results. Only rooms that are not already part of the specified team and that the user has permission to view will be returned.

output.summary: Autocomplete channel and private room names.
output.description: Returns a list of channel and private room names that match a given search term, useful for implementing autocomplete functionality in clients. This endpoint helps users quickly find and select channels or private groups by partial name. The search term is typically provided as a query parameter, and the response includes matching room information.

output.summary: Autocomplete admin rooms by name or ID.
output.description: Returns a list of rooms that match the given name or ID for administrative purposes. This endpoint is typically used to provide autocomplete suggestions when searching for rooms as an admin. You can filter results by partial room name or ID, and the response includes room details such as _id, name, and type. Requires appropriate admin permissions to access.

output.summary: Get autocomplete suggestions for admin rooms.
output.description: Provides autocomplete suggestions for room names that an admin can access. This endpoint is typically used to help administrators quickly find and select rooms by partial name or ID. The response may be filtered based on the admin's permissions and the input query. Exact usage and required parameters may depend on your Rocket.Chat server version and configuration.

output.summary: Retrieve information about a specific room as an admin.
output.description: Retrieves detailed information about a room by its ID, including its name, type, user count, and other properties. This endpoint requires the 'view-room-administration' permission and is intended for administrative use. The 'rid' query parameter (room ID) is required.

output.summary: Update settings for a room.
output.description: Update one or more settings for a specific room by providing the room ID, the setting key, and the new value. This endpoint allows you to change various room properties, such as enabling or disabling system messages and other configurable options. The available settings may vary depending on your Rocket.Chat server version and configuration. Appropriate permissions are required to modify room settings.

output.summary: Check if a room name exists.
output.description: Checks whether a room with the specified name already exists in the workspace. This endpoint is useful for validating room names before creating or renaming a room to avoid conflicts. Provide the room name as a parameter in the request. The response will indicate whether the name is already taken or available for use.

output.summary: Check if a room name exists.
output.description: Checks whether a room with the specified name already exists in the workspace. This endpoint is useful for validating room names before creating new channels or groups to avoid naming conflicts. Provide the room name as a query parameter (e.g., ?roomName=example). The response will indicate whether the name is already taken or available for use.

output.summary: Change the archived state of a room.
output.description: Change the archived (archivation) state of a room by archiving or unarchiving it. This endpoint likely requires the room ID and a boolean indicating whether to archive or unarchive the room. Use this to programmatically archive a room (making it read-only and hidden from lists) or unarchive it (restoring normal access). Note: Official documentation for this endpoint is not available, so parameter details may vary depending on your Rocket.Chat version.

output.summary: Export the contents of a room.
output.description: Exports the data of a specified room, such as messages and files, typically in a downloadable format. This endpoint may require special permissions and is often used for compliance, backup, or migration purposes. Details about required parameters and response format may vary depending on your Rocket.Chat server version and configuration.

output.summary: Mute a user in a room.
output.description: Mutes a specified user in a given room, preventing them from sending messages. Requires appropriate permissions. The request typically includes the room ID and the username or user ID to mute. Only users with permission to mute others in the room can perform this action.

output.summary: Unmute a user in a room.
output.description: Unmutes a previously muted user in a specific room. You must provide the room ID and the username of the user to unmute. The authenticated user must have permission to unmute users in the room. This endpoint is useful for restoring a user's ability to send messages after they have been muted.

output.summary: Create a discussion in a room.
output.description: Creates a new discussion thread within an existing room. You must specify the parent room and can optionally set the discussion name, users to include, and other properties. This endpoint is useful for organizing conversations around specific topics within a channel or group.

output.summary: Retrieve images shared in a room.
output.description: Fetches a list of images that have been shared in a specified room. This endpoint allows you to view all image files posted in the room, and may support pagination or filtering by date or user. Authentication is required, and you must have permission to view the room's contents.

output.summary: List parameters for retrieving room member audit logs.
output.description: Returns the available parameters that can be used when querying the /api/v1/audit/rooms.members endpoint. This helps users understand what filters and options are supported for retrieving audit logs of room members, such as filtering by user, room, or date range.

output.summary: Retrieve the list of members in a room for audit purposes.
output.description: Returns a list of members for a specified room, including user details and membership information, for auditing and compliance purposes. This endpoint is typically used by administrators to review room membership and track changes over time. Requires appropriate permissions to access audit data.

output.summary: Get members of a room ordered by role.
output.description: Retrieves a list of members in a specified room, ordered by their roles such as owner, moderator, and user. You typically need to provide the roomId or roomName as a parameter. The response includes user details and their roles within the room, allowing you to easily identify the hierarchy or permissions of each member. This endpoint is useful for managing room permissions or displaying role-based member lists.

output.summary: Get members of a room ordered by their role.
output.description: Retrieves a list of members in a specified room, ordered by their role hierarchy (e.g., owners, moderators, users, etc). This endpoint is useful for displaying or managing room participants according to their permissions or responsibilities. You must provide the room ID or name as a parameter. Pagination and filtering options may be available depending on the server version. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Create a new team.
output.description: Creates a new team in Rocket.Chat. You can specify the team name, members, and other options. The endpoint allows you to set team properties and optionally add users to the team during creation. Requires appropriate permissions to use.

output.summary: List all teams in the workspace.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all teams in the workspace, regardless of the user's membership. This endpoint is typically used for administrative purposes and may require special permissions. The response includes details for each team, such as team ID, name, and other metadata. Use this endpoint to audit, manage, or report on all teams within your Rocket.Chat instance.

output.summary: List all teams visible to the user.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all teams that the authenticated user can see. The response includes team details and supports pagination and filtering options. This endpoint is useful for displaying available teams or managing team memberships. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Get information about a team.
output.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific team, including its name, type, members, and other metadata. You must provide either the team's ID or name as a parameter. Authentication is required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Update a team's name or type.
output.description: Updates an existing team's name and/or type (public or private). You must provide the team ID and the new data (name and/or type). Permission required: edit-team. The type field uses 0 for public and 1 for private teams.

output.summary: Add members to a team.
output.description: Adds one or more users to a team by team ID or name. Requires the 'add-team-member' or 'edit-team-member' permission. You must provide the teamId (or teamName) and a list of members (user IDs and optional roles) to add. Authentication is required.

output.summary: List all members of a team.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all members belonging to a specified team. You can filter the results by team name or team ID, and optionally by user name, username, or status. The endpoint requires the 'view-all-teams' permission. The response includes user details, roles, and supports pagination with count and offset parameters.

output.summary: Update a team member's role or status in a team.
output.description: Updates the role or status of a member within a team. This endpoint allows you to promote, demote, or change the status (such as active or removed) of a user in a team. You must have appropriate permissions to perform this action. The request typically requires the team ID and the user ID, along with the new role or status to be set.

output.summary: Leave a team.
output.description: Removes the authenticated user from the specified team. The request typically requires the team ID or name in the body. After calling this endpoint, the user will no longer be a member of the team or its associated rooms. Only the authenticated user can remove themselves from a team using this endpoint.

output.summary: Remove a member from a team.
output.description: Removes a user from a team. You must provide the team ID or name and the user ID or username of the member to remove. The authenticated user must have appropriate permissions to remove members from the team. This action will revoke the user's access to all team channels unless they are added individually to those channels.

output.summary: Delete a team from the workspace.
output.description: Removes a team from the workspace. You must provide either the teamId or teamName. Optionally, you can specify roomsToRemove to delete specific rooms along with the team. The user must have the 'delete-team' permission to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Get autocomplete suggestions for teams.
output.description: Retrieves a list of team names that match a given search term, helping users to autocomplete team names when creating or searching for teams. This endpoint is useful for building UI elements that require team name suggestions as the user types. Typically, you provide a partial team name as a query parameter, and the API returns matching teams. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Convert a team to a channel.
output.description: Convert a team to a channel. This endpoint requires the 'convert-team' permission. You must provide the teamId of the team you want to convert. After conversion, the team will become a regular channel and will no longer have team-specific features.

output.summary: Add rooms to a team.
output.description: Adds one or more rooms to an existing team. You must provide the teamId and a list of room IDs to add. The user must have appropriate permissions to manage the team and the rooms. This endpoint is useful for organizing multiple rooms under a single team structure in Rocket.Chat.

output.summary: Remove a room from a team.
output.description: Removes a room from a team. You must provide either the teamId or teamName, and the roomId to be removed. The required permissions are 'remove-team-channel' and 'view-all-team-channels'. On success, the room is no longer associated with the team but is not deleted from the workspace.

output.summary: Update a room within a team.
output.description: Update the details of a room that belongs to a team, such as its name, topic, or other properties. This endpoint allows you to modify room attributes within the context of a team. You must have the appropriate permissions to update the room, and the request body should specify the room and the fields to update.

output.summary: List all rooms in a team.
output.description: Retrieves all rooms that belong to a specified team. You can filter by teamId or teamName, and optionally by room type. Requires the 'view-all-teams' or 'view-all-team-channels' permission. The response includes an array of room objects with details such as name, type, and user count.

output.summary: List all rooms a user belongs to within teams.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all rooms that a specified user is a member of within teams. You must provide the user's ID or username as a parameter. This endpoint is useful for administrators or integrations that need to audit or display a user's team room memberships. Appropriate permissions are required to access another user's room list. The response includes details about each room, such as its type and team association.

output.summary: List rooms and discussions of a team.
output.description: Lists a particular team's public rooms, discussions, and the rooms (public/private) a user is part of from the team's main room. You can filter by type (channels or discussions) and by text. The endpoint currently returns discussions from the parent team room only, not from sub-channels. Either teamId, teamName, or roomId is required as a parameter. Pagination and sorting are supported.

output.summary: Get a list of online users in a private group.
output.description: Retrieves a list of users who are currently online in a specified private group. You must provide the group ID or name as a query parameter. This endpoint requires authentication and appropriate permissions to access the group information. Useful for monitoring group activity or presence status within private groups.

output.summary: List integrations for a private group.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all integrations (such as incoming and outgoing webhooks, bots, etc.) associated with a specified private group. You must provide the group ID or name as a parameter. The response includes details about each integration. Appropriate permissions are required to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Add all users to a private group.
output.description: Adds all users in the workspace to the specified private group. This endpoint is useful for quickly populating a group with all users. You must have the appropriate permissions to perform this action. Existing group members will not be duplicated. Use with caution, especially in workspaces with a large number of users, as this may impact performance or group usability.

output.summary: Assign the leader role to a user in a private group.
output.description: Grants a specified user the leader role in a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and the user's ID or username. The user will gain leader permissions for the group, which may include managing group settings and members. Appropriate permissions are required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Add a moderator to a private group.
output.description: Assigns the moderator role to a user in a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and the user ID or username to be made a moderator. The authenticated user must have permission to manage roles in the group. This endpoint is useful for managing group permissions and access control within private groups.

output.summary: Assign the owner role to a user in a private group.
output.description: Assigns the 'owner' role to a user in a private group (also known as a private channel). Requires the roomId of the group and the userId of the user to be promoted. The user will gain owner permissions for the group. See the Rocket.Chat documentation on roles for more details.

output.summary: Archive a private group (channel)
output.description: Archives a private group (also known as a private channel) in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint requires the 'archive-room' permission. You must provide the group ID (roomId) of the private group you want to archive. Once archived, the group will be read-only and hidden from the list of active groups, but its history will be preserved. Only users with the appropriate permissions can archive or unarchive groups.

output.summary: Close a private group.
output.description: Closes a private group, making it inaccessible to its members until it is reopened. This endpoint is typically used to archive or temporarily disable access to a group. Only users with the appropriate permissions can close a group.

output.summary: Get counters for a private group.
output.description: Retrieves various counters and statistics for a private group, such as the number of unread messages, mentions, and total messages. You must provide either the groupId or roomId as a query parameter. This endpoint is useful for displaying group activity indicators in clients. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Create a private group (private channel)
output.description: Creates a new private group (also known as a private channel) in Rocket.Chat. You can specify the group's name, include users by username, and set additional options such as read-only status or custom fields. This endpoint is useful for creating private spaces for team collaboration that are not visible to all users. Authentication is required, and the user must have permission to create groups.

output.summary: Delete a private group.
output.description: Deletes a private group (also known as a private channel) from the workspace. This endpoint requires authentication and appropriate permissions. You must provide the group ID or name in the request body. Once deleted, the group and its messages cannot be recovered. Use with caution.

output.summary: Retrieve the message history of a private group.
output.description: Fetches the messages from a private group (also known as a private channel) in Rocket.Chat. You must be a member of the group to access its history. Supports query parameters such as roomId, latest, oldest, inclusive, count, and unreads to filter and paginate results. Useful for retrieving chat history, searching for specific messages, or implementing custom message viewers. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Get information about a private group.
output.description: Retrieves information about a private group (also known as a private channel) in RocketChat. You must provide either the group's unique ID or name as a parameter. The response includes details such as the group's name, members, topic, and other metadata. Authentication is required, and the user must be a member of the group or have appropriate permissions to access its information.

output.summary: Invite a user to a private group.
output.description: Adds a user to a private group by specifying the group and user to invite. The authenticated user must have permission to add members to the group. Typically, you provide the group ID or name and the user ID or username in the request body.

output.summary: Remove a user from a private group.
output.description: Removes a specified user from a private group. You must provide the group ID and the user ID to remove. The authenticated user must have permission to remove users from the group. This action will immediately revoke the user's access to the group and its messages.

output.summary: Leave a private group.
output.description: Removes the authenticated user from a private group (also known as a private channel). The user will no longer receive messages or notifications from the group after leaving. Requires authentication. If the user is the last owner of the group, they must assign another owner before leaving.

output.summary: List all private groups in the workspace.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all private groups (also known as private channels) in the workspace, regardless of membership. This endpoint may require special permissions, such as view-room-administration, to access groups the user is not a member of. Useful for administrative tasks or integrations that need visibility into all private groups. The response includes group details such as name, ID, and other metadata.

output.summary: List all private groups that the user is part of.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all private groups (also known as private channels) that the authenticated user is a member of. The response includes group details such as name, ID, and other metadata. Pagination and filtering options may be available via query parameters. The user must be authenticated to use this endpoint.

output.summary: List all members of a private group.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all members in a specified private group. You must provide the group ID or name as a parameter. The response includes user details for each member. Pagination and filtering options may be available. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve messages from a private group.
output.description: Fetches the messages from a private group (also known as a private channel) in Rocket.Chat. You must be a member of the group to access its messages. Supports pagination and additional query parameters such as 'roomId', 'count', 'offset', and 'query' to filter or limit the results. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Get the list of moderators for a private group.
output.description: Retrieves all users who have the moderator role in a specified private group. You must provide the group ID or name as a parameter. Authentication is required to use this endpoint. The response includes user details for each moderator in the group.

output.summary: Open a private group that has been archived.
output.description: Reopens a private group (direct message room) that was previously archived. This endpoint allows users to restore access to the group and resume activity. The user must have appropriate permissions to open the group. The group must already exist and be in an archived state.

output.summary: Remove a user as a leader from a private group.
output.description: Removes the leader role from a specified user in a private group. The request must include the group ID or name and the user ID or username to be demoted. The requester must have appropriate permissions to manage group roles.

output.summary: Remove a moderator from a private group.
output.description: Removes the moderator role from a specified user in a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and the username of the user to be demoted. The authenticated user must have appropriate permissions to manage roles in the group.

output.summary: Remove the owner role from a user in a private group.
output.description: Removes the owner role from a specified user in a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and the username of the user to be demoted. The requester must have appropriate permissions to manage group roles. This action does not remove the user from the group, only their owner status.

output.summary: Rename a private group.
output.description: Renames an existing private group (also known as a private channel) to a new name. You must provide the group ID and the new name. The user must have appropriate permissions to rename the group.

output.summary: Set the announcement for a private group.
output.description: Sets or updates the announcement text for a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and the new announcement text. Only users with the appropriate permissions can change the announcement. The updated announcement will be visible to all group members.

output.summary: Set custom fields for a private group.
output.description: Sets or updates custom fields for a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and a customFields object in the request body. This endpoint allows you to store additional metadata for the group, which can be used for integrations or custom workflows. Requires appropriate permissions to modify group information.

output.summary: Set the description for a private group.
output.description: Updates the description of a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and the new description. The user must have permission to edit the group. This endpoint is useful for updating group information visible to members.

output.summary: Set the purpose of a private group.
output.description: Sets or updates the purpose (description) of a private group. You must provide the group ID or name and the new purpose text. Only users with appropriate permissions can change the group's purpose. The updated purpose will be visible to all group members.

output.summary: Set a private group as read-only or writable.
output.description: Sets a private group (also known as a private channel) to be read-only or writable. Requires the 'edit-room' permission. You must provide the group ID (roomId) and a boolean value for readOnly. When a group is set to read-only, only users with appropriate permissions can send messages. The group ID can be obtained using endpoints such as 'Get List of User Groups' or 'Get Groups'.

output.summary: Set the topic for a private group (private channel)
output.description: Sets the topic for a private group (private channel). You must provide the group ID (roomId) and the new topic. The user must have the 'edit-room' permission for the group. This endpoint is useful for updating or clarifying the subject of discussion in a private group.

output.summary: Change the type of a private group.
output.description: Changes the type of a private group to either public or private. You must specify the group and the desired type in the request. This endpoint is useful for converting a private group to a public channel or vice versa. Appropriate permissions are required to perform this action.

output.summary: Unarchive a private group.
output.description: Unarchives a previously archived private group, making it active and accessible again. The user must have the appropriate permissions to unarchive the group. Provide the group ID or name in the request body to specify which group to unarchive.

output.summary: List files shared in a private group.
output.description: Retrieves a list of files that have been shared in a specific private group. You must provide the group ID or name as a parameter. The response includes file metadata such as name, type, size, and uploader. Pagination parameters can be used to limit results. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Set a private group as encrypted.
output.description: Set a private group (private channel) as encrypted or unencrypted. This endpoint allows you to enable or disable end-to-end encryption for a private group by specifying the group ID or name and the desired encryption state. Permission required: 'edit-room'. For more information about end-to-end encryption, see the Rocket.Chat documentation.

output.summary: Convert a private group to a team.
output.description: Converts an existing private group (group chat) into a team. This operation changes the room type and may affect permissions, visibility, and how the group is managed. Only users with the appropriate permissions can perform this action.

output.summary: Get the roles of users in a private group.
output.description: Retrieves the list of roles assigned to users within a specific private group (also known as a group or private channel). You must provide the group ID or name as a parameter. The response includes user IDs and their corresponding roles in the group. This endpoint requires appropriate permissions to view group roles.

output.summary: Search for users or channels in the directory.
output.description: This endpoint allows you to search the directory for users or channels (public rooms) in Rocket.Chat. You can filter results by type (users or channels) and provide a search text. Additional query parameters may be available to refine your search. The response includes matching users or channels with relevant details.

output.summary: Hide a room from the user's list of rooms.
output.description: Hides a room (channel, group, or direct message) from the authenticated user's list of rooms. This does not delete or leave the room; it simply removes it from view until the user accesses it again. Useful for decluttering the room list without affecting membership or message history. Requires authentication.

output.summary: Specify parameters for closing a chat or performing handover via a public app endpoint.
output.description: This endpoint is used to close a chat session or perform a handover action for a public app, such as the Rasa app, in Rocket.Chat. The required parameters include the app ID (app-id), the action to perform (either 'handover' or 'close-chat'), and the session ID. Optionally, you can provide additional action data such as the target department. The full endpoint URL, including the app ID, can be found in the App Info > Details > APIs > POST incoming section of the app. This endpoint is typically used by marketplace apps to manage chat sessions programmatically.

output.summary: Send incoming data to a public app by app ID.
output.description: Allows external services to send data or events to a specific public Rocket.Chat app using its app ID. The app must be configured to handle incoming requests at this endpoint. This is typically used for integrations such as webhooks or external triggers. Ensure the app is prepared to process the incoming payload according to its logic and security requirements.

output.summary: Send a template message using a public app.
output.description: Sends a template message, such as a WhatsApp template, using the specified public app identified by appId. The app must support template messaging and be installed from the Rocket.Chat Marketplace. This endpoint is typically used for apps that integrate with external messaging platforms and require sending pre-approved template messages. Ensure the appId corresponds to a valid public app with template messaging capabilities.

output.summary: Install a private app via URL or file upload.
output.description: Install a private app in your Rocket.Chat workspace by providing either a URL to the app's zip file or uploading the zip file directly. You must have the 'manage-apps' permission to use this endpoint. You can also specify the permissions required by your app if they are defined in the app.json file. Either the 'app' or 'url' parameter is required to upload the app.

output.summary: Retrieve logs for all installed apps.
output.description: Use this endpoint to get the list of logs for all apps installed in your workspace. You can filter logs by app ID, log level, method, date range, and more using query parameters. The response includes details such as log entries, severity, timestamps, and execution times. Permission required: `manage-apps`.

output.summary: Retrieve logs for a specific app.
output.description: Use this endpoint to get the logs for a specific app in your workspace by providing the app ID. You can filter logs by method, log level, date range, and pagination parameters. The 'manage-apps' permission is required to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Create an incoming or outgoing integration (webhook)
output.description: Creates a new incoming or outgoing integration (webhook) in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint allows you to configure webhooks that can either receive data from external services (incoming) or send data to external services (outgoing) based on events in Rocket.Chat. Required fields include the type (webhook-incoming or webhook-outgoing), username, channel, scriptEnabled, name, enabled, and for outgoing integrations, event and urls. Permissions required: manage-incoming-integrations/manage-own-incoming-integrations for incoming, and manage-outgoing-integrations/manage-own-outgoing-integrations for outgoing.

output.summary: Retrieve a list of integrations configured in the workspace.
output.description: Fetches details of all integrations (such as incoming and outgoing webhooks) set up in the Rocket.Chat workspace. This endpoint may support filtering by type or user and typically requires the user to have appropriate permissions to view integrations. The response includes configuration details for each integration, which can be used for management or auditing purposes.

output.summary: Retrieve the history of a specific integration.
output.description: Retrieves the execution history for a given integration by its ID. Requires one of the following permissions: manage-incoming-integrations, manage-own-incoming-integrations, manage-outgoing-integrations, or manage-own-outgoing-integrations. Supports pagination and filtering via query parameters. The response includes an array of history records for the specified integration, along with pagination details.

output.summary: Retrieve a list of all integrations.
output.description: Returns a list of all integrations (such as incoming and outgoing webhooks, bots, etc.) configured in the Rocket.Chat workspace that the authenticated user has access to. This endpoint may support filtering or pagination options. Appropriate permissions are required to access the list of integrations.

output.summary: Update an existing integration.
output.description: Updates the details of an existing integration, such as a webhook or bot integration, in your Rocket.Chat workspace. You must provide the integration ID and the new configuration parameters in the request body. Authentication and appropriate permissions are required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Remove an existing integration.
output.description: Removes an existing integration (such as an incoming or outgoing webhook or bot integration) from the Rocket.Chat server. You must provide the integration's unique ID in the request body. Only users with the appropriate permissions can remove integrations. This action is irreversible and will immediately disable the integration's functionality.

output.summary: Retrieve the list of your connected WebDAV accounts.
output.description: Returns all WebDAV accounts that are connected to the authenticated user. This endpoint allows you to view the external storage accounts you have integrated with Rocket.Chat via WebDAV. Authentication is required to access this information.

output.summary: Remove a WebDAV account integration.
output.description: Removes a WebDAV account integration from the authenticated user's account. This endpoint is used to disconnect a previously added WebDAV account, preventing further access to files from that account through Rocket.Chat. The request typically requires the account ID or relevant identifier in the request body. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Register a new OAuth application for integrations.
output.description: Creates a new OAuth application (client) in Rocket.Chat, allowing administrators to register external applications that can authenticate and integrate with the workspace. You can specify details such as the application's name, redirect URIs, and permissions. This endpoint is typically used to enable third-party integrations that require OAuth authentication. Only users with the appropriate permissions can create OAuth apps.

output.summary: Update an existing OAuth application.
output.description: Updates the details of an existing OAuth application registered in Rocket.Chat. You must provide the OAuth app's unique identifier and the new values for the fields you wish to update, such as name, redirect URI, or other configuration options. Authentication is required, and administrative permissions may be necessary to perform this action.

output.summary: List all OAuth applications.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all OAuth applications registered in the Rocket.Chat workspace. This endpoint is typically used by administrators to view details about each OAuth app, such as name, client ID, and other metadata. Authentication and appropriate permissions may be required to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Retrieve information about an OAuth app.
output.description: Retrieves an OAuth app by its ID or client ID. Requires the 'manage-oauth-apps' permission to view all details, but can be accessed without this permission with sensitive information (such as client secrets) filtered out. You must provide either the appId, clientId, or _id as a query parameter. Note: The 'appId' parameter will be deprecated from version 7.0.0; use 'clientId' or '_id' instead.

output.summary: Delete an OAuth application.
output.description: Deletes an existing OAuth application from the Rocket.Chat server. You must provide the OAuth app's ID in the request body. Only users with the appropriate permissions can perform this action. This operation is irreversible and will remove all associated credentials and access for the deleted OAuth app.

output.summary: Get public settings parameters.
output.description: Retrieves the parameters for public settings. This endpoint allows you to view the values of all public settings that are available to unauthenticated users or the general public. It is useful for clients or integrations that need to access configuration values that do not require authentication. No authentication is required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Retrieve all public workspace settings.
output.description: Returns all public (non-sensitive) settings configured for the Rocket.Chat workspace. This endpoint is typically used by clients to obtain configuration values that are safe to expose, such as site name, branding, or feature toggles. No authentication is required, and only settings marked as public by the server administrator will be included in the response.

output.summary: Manage OAuth settings parameters.
output.description: Retrieve or update the parameters related to OAuth settings in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint allows you to configure OAuth providers, manage their credentials, and adjust authentication options for third-party login integrations. Use this endpoint to ensure proper setup of external authentication services such as Google, GitHub, or custom OAuth providers.

output.summary: Retrieve the current OAuth settings.
output.description: Returns the current OAuth configuration for the Rocket.Chat workspace, including enabled OAuth providers, their settings, and any custom OAuth methods. This endpoint is useful for administrators or integrations that need to view or audit the available OAuth authentication options and their configuration details.

output.summary: Get the parameters for the /api/v1/settings endpoint.
output.description: This endpoint provides the list of parameters that can be used with the /api/v1/settings endpoint. It helps users understand what query or body parameters are accepted when interacting with the settings API, including their names, types, and possible values. This is useful for building dynamic clients or for documentation purposes.

output.summary: Get a list of all public settings.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all public settings from the Rocket.Chat server. This endpoint can be used to view the current configuration values that are not marked as hidden or private. Pagination and filtering options may be available to limit the results. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Add a custom OAuth provider to Rocket.Chat.
output.description: Registers a new custom OAuth provider in your Rocket.Chat workspace. This endpoint allows administrators to configure external OAuth authentication by specifying provider details such as name, client ID, client secret, authorization URL, token URL, and user info endpoint. Proper configuration enables users to log in using the new OAuth provider. Only accessible to users with appropriate administrative permissions.

output.summary: Add a custom OAuth service configuration.
output.description: Adds a new custom OAuth service configuration to Rocket.Chat. This endpoint allows administrators to define and register a new OAuth provider by specifying its settings, such as client ID, secret, URLs, and other required parameters. Proper configuration is necessary for successful authentication integration. Only users with appropriate permissions can use this endpoint.

output.summary: Get the parameters for a specific setting by ID.
output.description: Retrieve the parameters and details for a specific setting using its unique ID. This endpoint is useful for obtaining metadata or configuration options related to a particular setting in Rocket.Chat. The {_id} path parameter should be replaced with the setting's unique identifier. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Update a setting by its ID.
output.description: Updates the value of a specific setting identified by its unique ID. This endpoint is typically used by administrators to change configuration options in the workspace. The request body should include the new value for the setting. Proper permissions are required to use this endpoint, and the setting ID must be valid and known in advance.

output.summary: Get details of a setting by ID.
output.description: Retrieve the details of a specific setting by its unique ID. This endpoint requires the 'view-privileged-setting' permission and returns the setting's current value. The setting ID corresponds to the first argument of the Rocket.Chat.settings.add method.

output.summary: Get the parameters for the service configurations endpoint.
output.description: Returns the list of parameters accepted by the /api/v1/service.configurations endpoint, including details about each parameter such as name, type, and description. This information helps you understand what parameters can be used when interacting with the service configurations API.

output.summary: Retrieve all active OAuth service configurations.
output.description: Lists all the active OAuth services configured in the workspace, including details such as service name and client ID. This endpoint is useful for administrators who need to audit or manage external authentication providers. The response includes an array of configuration objects for each OAuth service currently set up.

output.summary: Retrieve the audit history of changed settings.
output.description: Retrieve a list of all changes made to workspace settings within a specified time period. This endpoint is useful for auditing purposes and allows filtering by time range, setting ID, actor, and other parameters. Requires the 'can-audit' permission. Returned data includes details about the change, who made it, when, and the previous and current values of the setting.

output.summary: Retrieve the history of changed settings for auditing purposes.
output.description: Get a list of all settings that have been changed within a specified time period, including details about who made the change, when it was made, and what the previous and current values were. This endpoint is useful for auditing configuration changes in your Rocket.Chat workspace. You can filter results by time range, setting ID, actor, and more. Permission required: can-audit.

output.summary: Manually register a workspace on Rocket.Chat Cloud.
output.description: Manually register a workspace on Rocket.Chat Cloud. This endpoint requires the 'register-on-cloud' permission and a 'cloudBlob' value in the request body, which represents the workspace deployment ID. Use this endpoint if automatic registration is not possible. If the workspace is already registered or required data is missing, an error will be returned.

output.summary: Manually register your workspace with Rocket.Chat Cloud.
output.description: This endpoint allows you to manually register your Rocket.Chat workspace with Rocket.Chat Cloud. Registration is required to enable cloud services, manage licenses, and access cloud-only features. You may need to provide organization and workspace details in the request body. Use this endpoint if automatic registration is not possible or if you need to re-register your workspace for cloud integration.

output.summary: Resolve DNS TXT records for a hostname.
output.description: Resolves DNS text records (TXT records) for a specified hostname. This endpoint requires authentication and expects the hostname to be provided as a query parameter named 'url'. The response will include the TXT records found for the given hostname, or an error if the lookup fails.

output.summary: Resolve DNS TXT records for a hostname.
output.description: Resolves DNS text records (TXT records) for a specified hostname. You must provide the hostname as the 'url' query parameter. The endpoint returns the TXT records found for the given hostname. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Resolve SRV DNS records for a given domain.
output.description: This endpoint allows you to resolve SRV (Service) DNS records for a specified domain. It returns the SRV records found, which can be useful for discovering service hosts and ports for protocols that use SRV records. You must provide the domain and service details as parameters. The response includes the priority, weight, port, and target for each SRV record found.

output.summary: Resolve DNS SRV records for a hostname.
output.description: Resolves DNS SRV (service) records for a given hostname. You must provide the hostname as the 'url' parameter in the request body. The response will indicate whether the lookup was successful or not, and will include any errors if the query fails. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Fetch the user's E2E encryption keys.
output.description: Retrieves the end-to-end (E2E) encryption keys for the authenticated user. This endpoint is used to obtain the user's E2E keys, which are necessary for decrypting encrypted messages and for secure communication. The user must be authenticated to access their keys.

output.summary: Fetch the current user's E2E encryption keys.
output.description: Retrieves the end-to-end (E2E) encryption keys for the authenticated user. This endpoint is used to obtain the user's public and private E2E keys, which are necessary for encrypted messaging features. Authentication is required, and the response will include the user's E2E key data if available.

output.summary: Get users in a room without an end-to-end encryption key.
output.description: Retrieves a list of users in a specified room who have not set up their end-to-end encryption (E2E) key. This can be useful for administrators or clients to identify users who need to configure E2E encryption for secure messaging. Typically, you must provide the room ID as a parameter. Ensure you have the necessary permissions to access this information.

output.summary: Get users in a room without E2E encryption keys.
output.description: Retrieves a list of users in a specified room who have not yet set up their end-to-end (E2E) encryption keys. This endpoint is useful for monitoring E2E encryption adoption and prompting users to enable encryption for secure communication. Typically, you must provide the room ID as a parameter. Only users with appropriate permissions can access this information.

output.summary: Set the E2E room key ID for a room.
output.description: Sets the end-to-end encryption (E2E) key ID for a specific room. This endpoint is used to update or assign the E2E key identifier for a room, which is necessary for managing encrypted communications. Proper authentication is required to use this endpoint, and the request must include the room ID and the new key ID.

output.summary: Set the E2E encryption key ID for a room.
output.description: Sets or updates the end-to-end encryption (E2E) key ID for a specific room. This endpoint is used by clients to manage encryption keys for secure messaging, such as when initializing E2E encryption or rotating keys. Proper use of this endpoint is essential for maintaining secure communications in encrypted rooms.

output.summary: Set a user's E2E public and private keys.
output.description: Sets the end-to-end (E2E) encryption public and private keys for the authenticated user. This endpoint is used to store the user's E2E key pair on the server, which is required for encrypted messaging. The keys should be generated securely on the client side and never shared with others. Only the authenticated user can set their own keys using this endpoint.

output.summary: Set a user's E2E public and private keys.
output.description: Sets the end-to-end encryption (E2E) public and private keys for the authenticated user. This endpoint is used to update or register the user's E2E key pair, which is required for secure encrypted messaging. The keys should be generated and managed securely on the client side before being sent to this endpoint.

output.summary: Update the end-to-end encryption group key for a room.
output.description: Updates the group key used for end-to-end encryption in a specific room. This endpoint is typically used when the group membership changes or when a new encryption key needs to be distributed to room members. Proper authentication and permissions are required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Upload an import file for workspace data migration.
output.description: Uploads a file to be used for importing data into Rocket.Chat, such as users, channels, or messages. The request must include the file's binary content, the importer key (e.g., 'csv', 'slack', 'pending-avatars'), the file name, and the content type (MIME type). The file is stored in a buffer for later processing by the import operation. Permission required: 'run-import'.

output.summary: Upload an import file for processing.
output.description: Uploads a file to be imported into Rocket.Chat, along with metadata such as the file name, content type, and importer key (e.g., csv, slack, hipchatenterprise, pending-avatars, pending-files, slack-users). The file is stored in a buffer for later processing. Permission required: run-import. Required fields: binaryContent (file data), importerKey (import type), fileName, and contentType (MIME type).

output.summary: Download a public import file for workspace import.
output.description: Download a public import file from a specified URL for use in workspace import operations. The request must include the fileUrl (which must start with http or https) and an importerKey indicating how Rocket.Chat should handle the file (accepted values: csv, hipchatenterprise, pending-avatars, pending-files, slack, slack-users). Permission required: run-import.

output.summary: Download a public import file for data import.
output.description: Downloads a public import file from a specified URL and stores it for use in the import process. The request must include the fileUrl (which must start with http or https) and an importerKey indicating how Rocket.Chat should handle the file (accepted values: csv, hipchatenterprise, pending-avatars, pending-files, slack, slack-users). Permission 'run-import' is required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Get the parameters required to start an import operation.
output.description: Retrieve the list of parameters and their expected values needed to initiate an import process in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint helps you understand what information must be provided to successfully start an import, such as file types, required fields, and any other configuration options. Use this before calling the actual import start endpoint to ensure all prerequisites are met.

output.summary: Start a data import process.
output.description: Initiates the import process for previously uploaded data files, such as user, room, and message data from other platforms (e.g., Slack, HipChat, or CSV). This endpoint is typically used after uploading an import file and selecting the import type. It is part of the workspace administration tools for data migration and may require specifying import options depending on the source.

output.summary: Retrieve data from the uploaded import file.
output.description: Fetches the users, channels, and message count contained in the uploaded import file for an import operation. This endpoint is used after uploading an import file to preview its contents before starting the import process. Permission required: run-import.

output.summary: Retrieve data from the imported file for review before import.
output.description: Fetches the users, channels, and message count from the uploaded import file, allowing you to review the data that will be imported into Rocket.Chat. This endpoint requires the 'run-import' permission and is typically used after uploading an import file but before starting the import process.

output.summary: Get the progress of an ongoing import operation.
output.description: Retrieves the current progress and status of an active import process in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint is useful for monitoring the state of data imports, such as user or message imports, and provides information about the number of items processed, errors encountered, and overall completion percentage. No parameters are required.

output.summary: Get the progress of an import operation.
output.description: Retrieve the current progress of an ongoing import operation, including the step, completed and total items, and other details. This endpoint requires the 'run-import' permission and is useful for tracking the status of user, room, or message imports in Rocket.Chat.

output.summary: Get parameters for the latest import operations.
output.description: Retrieve the parameters used for the most recent import operations. This endpoint is useful for auditing or troubleshooting import settings and can help administrators review the configuration of previous import jobs.

output.summary: Retrieve the latest import operations.
output.description: Fetches the most recent import operations performed in the workspace, including details such as operation type, status, user, and timestamps. This endpoint requires the 'view-import-operations' permission and is useful for tracking the status and history of recent import activities.

output.summary: Download files pending in the system.
output.description: Triggers the download of files that are pending in the Rocket.Chat system, such as files awaiting synchronization or migration. This endpoint may be undocumented or internal, and its usage or required permissions may vary depending on your Rocket.Chat version. Use with caution and consult your server administrator or Rocket.Chat support for more details.

output.summary: Download all pending files on the server.
output.description: Triggers the download of all files currently marked as pending on the server. This endpoint is typically used to retry or resume downloads for files that have not yet been successfully downloaded, often for administrative or maintenance purposes. Authentication and appropriate permissions may be required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Get parameters for downloading pending avatars.
output.description: Retrieves the parameters required to download avatars that are pending in the system. This endpoint is typically used to obtain information necessary for clients or integrations to fetch and process user avatars that have not yet been downloaded or updated. Ensure you have the appropriate permissions to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Download all pending user avatars.
output.description: Triggers the download of all user avatars that are pending, such as avatars set by users that have not yet been fetched from external sources. This endpoint is typically used to ensure that all user avatars are up to date in the workspace. It may require administrative permissions. Use this endpoint if you need to manually fetch or update avatars that are awaiting download.

output.summary: Get the parameters for the current import operation.
output.description: Retrieves the parameters and status of the currently running import operation, if any. This endpoint is useful for monitoring the progress and configuration of an ongoing import process in Rocket.Chat. It returns details such as the type of import, its current state, and any relevant settings or options that were specified when the import was started. If no import is in progress, the response will indicate that as well.

output.summary: Get the status of the current import operation.
output.description: Retrieves information about the current data import operation in progress, such as its status, type, and progress details. This endpoint is useful for monitoring or troubleshooting ongoing imports (e.g., from Slack, HipChat, or CSV). Only one import operation can be active at a time.

output.summary: Get parameters for starting a new import operation.
output.description: Retrieve the required parameters and options for initiating a new import process in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint provides information about the available importers, supported file types, and any additional settings needed to start an import. Use this before calling the import start endpoint to ensure you provide all necessary data.

output.summary: Start a new data import operation.
output.description: Initiates a new import process in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint is used to begin importing data from supported sources, such as other chat platforms or backup files. You must provide the required import parameters in the request body. After starting the import, you can monitor its progress and manage the import process using related endpoints. Ensure you have the necessary permissions to perform import operations.
