output.summary: Add users for import via parameters.
output.description: Allows you to specify user data as parameters to be added for import into Rocket.Chat. This endpoint is typically used during the import process to queue users for later import, and expects user information in the request body. Make sure to provide the required user fields as specified in the import documentation.

output.summary: Add users for import into Rocket.Chat.
output.description: Adds a list of users to the import queue in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint is typically used during data migration or bulk user onboarding, allowing administrators to prepare user accounts for import. The request body should include user data in the required format. Ensure you have the necessary permissions to perform this action.

output.summary: Run an import operation with specified parameters.
output.description: Runs an import operation using the provided parameters. This endpoint is used to start an import process, such as importing data from another platform or backup, and requires the necessary parameters to be specified in the request. Make sure to provide all required fields for the import to execute successfully. Refer to the RocketChat import documentation for details on supported import types and parameter formats.

output.summary: Run the current import operation to create users.
output.description: Processes the data from the current import operation and creates users in Rocket.Chat. The import operation must be in the 'ready' state before this endpoint can be called, and it will transition the operation to 'importing'. The endpoint returns success if the import process starts successfully, but does not wait for completion. Users that cannot be imported (e.g., due to duplicate emails or usernames) will be flagged, but the operation will continue. Only successfully imported users are removed from the staging area. Permission required: 'run-import'.

output.summary: Get the parameters for the import status endpoint.
output.description: Returns the parameters required or accepted by the /api/v1/import.status endpoint. This can help you understand what information you need to provide when checking the status of an import operation in Rocket.Chat.

output.summary: Get the current import operation status.
output.description: Retrieves the current status of any ongoing or most recent import operation in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint provides information about the progress, errors, and other details related to data import processes. Useful for monitoring the state of imports and troubleshooting issues during data migration. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Clear all import operation parameters.
output.description: Removes all parameters and data related to the current import operation. Use this endpoint to reset the import process before starting a new import or if you want to discard the current import configuration. This action cannot be undone, so ensure you do not need the current import data before clearing.

output.summary: Clear all import operations and related data.
output.description: Removes all data related to previous import operations, including imported users, channels, and messages. This endpoint is useful for resetting the import state before starting a new import process. Use with caution, as this action is irreversible and will permanently delete all import-related data from the system. Administrator permissions are required to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Retrieve information about the Rocket.Chat instance(s)
output.description: Fetches details about the current Rocket.Chat instance or cluster, such as deployment information, version, and other relevant metadata. This endpoint is useful for administrators or integrations that need to programmatically access instance configuration or status. Authentication is typically required to access this endpoint.

output.summary: Retrieve all running instances for the workspace.
output.description: Get the list of all Rocket.Chat server instances currently running for the workspace, including their status, address, and system information. This endpoint requires the 'view-statistics' permission and is useful for monitoring and managing clustered or multi-instance deployments.

output.summary: Add a federated server by user request.
output.description: Allows a user to add a new federated server to the Rocket.Chat instance. This endpoint is typically used in federated environments to expand the network of trusted servers. Proper permissions may be required to perform this action, and the server address or relevant parameters must be provided in the request body.

output.summary: Add a federated server by user request.
output.description: Allows a user to add a new federated server to the Rocket.Chat instance. This endpoint is typically used to expand the federation network by specifying a remote server, enabling communication and interoperability between different Rocket.Chat servers. Proper permissions may be required to use this endpoint, and the server address or domain must be provided in the request body.

output.summary: List all federation servers associated with a user.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all federation servers that are associated with a specific user. This endpoint is useful for administrators or integrations that need to audit or manage which external servers a user is federated with. Authentication and appropriate permissions may be required to access this information.

output.summary: List federation servers by user.
output.description: Retrieves a list of federation servers associated with a specific user. This endpoint is useful for administrators or integrations that need to view which external servers a user is federated with. Authentication and appropriate permissions are required to access this information.

output.summary: Remove a federated server by user request.
output.description: Removes a federated server from the Rocket.Chat instance based on a user request. This endpoint is typically used in federation settings to allow users to initiate the removal of a remote server from the federation network. Proper permissions may be required to perform this action, and the request may need to specify the server to be removed.

output.summary: Remove a federated server by user request.
output.description: Removes a federated server from the workspace's federation configuration upon user request. This endpoint is typically used to disassociate a remote server from the current Rocket.Chat instance. Appropriate permissions may be required to perform this action, and the request may need to specify the server to be removed.

output.summary: Search for public rooms across federated Rocket.Chat servers.
output.description: This endpoint allows you to search for public rooms that are available on federated Rocket.Chat servers. It is useful for discovering and joining public rooms outside your local server within a federated network. You may need to provide search parameters such as room name or server domain. The exact parameters and response format may depend on your Rocket.Chat version and federation configuration.

output.summary: Search for public federated rooms across the Matrix network.
output.description: This endpoint allows you to search for public rooms available on federated Matrix servers from your Rocket.Chat workspace. You can specify a target server and search for rooms that are open to the public, making it easier to discover and join federated channels for cross-organization collaboration. This feature is available to workspaces on premium plans (from version 6.3). Note that joining very large rooms may require additional configuration on the Matrix server. Server management options allow you to add or remove Matrix servers from your search scope.

output.summary: Join an external public room via federation.
output.description: Allows a user to join a public room that exists on an external federated server. This endpoint is used in federated Rocket.Chat deployments to enable users to participate in public rooms hosted on other servers. You may need to provide the external room identifier and ensure that federation is properly configured on your server for this operation to succeed.

output.summary: Join a public room on a federated server.
output.description: Allows a user to join a public room that exists on an external Rocket.Chat server via federation. You must provide the identifier of the external public room and the domain of the remote server. This endpoint is useful for connecting users across different federated Rocket.Chat instances. Ensure that federation is properly configured on your server before using this endpoint.

output.summary: Retrieve parameters for the moderation reports by users endpoint.
output.description: Provides information about the parameters accepted by the /api/v1/moderation.reportsByUsers endpoint. Use this to understand what query or body parameters can be used when requesting reports submitted by users for moderation purposes. This is typically used to construct valid API requests for fetching user-submitted moderation reports.

output.summary: Retrieve moderation reports by users.
output.description: Fetches a list of moderation reports grouped or filtered by users. This endpoint allows administrators or moderators to review reported messages or activities associated with specific users. Access to this endpoint may require special permissions depending on your Rocket.Chat server configuration. For detailed usage and available query parameters, refer to your server's API documentation or contact your administrator.

output.summary: List parameters for retrieving reported user messages.
output.description: Returns the available parameters that can be used when querying the /api/v1/moderation.user.reportedMessages endpoint. This helps users understand what filters, sorting, or pagination options are supported when requesting reported messages for moderation purposes.

output.summary: Retrieve messages reported by users for moderation.
output.description: Fetches a list of messages that have been reported by users for moderation review. This endpoint is typically used by moderators or administrators to view and manage reported content. Access to this endpoint may require special permissions depending on your Rocket.Chat server configuration. The response usually includes details about the reported messages, such as the message content, reporting user, and reason for the report.

output.summary: List parameters for the moderation reports endpoint.
output.description: Retrieve the list of accepted parameters for the /api/v1/moderation.reports endpoint. This can help you understand what query or body parameters are available and required when interacting with the moderation reports API.

output.summary: Retrieve moderation reports.
output.description: Retrieves a list of reported messages and users for moderation purposes. This endpoint allows administrators and moderators to review reports of inappropriate content or behavior, view details about reported messages and users, and take appropriate actions such as dismissing reports, deleting messages, or deactivating users. Filtering and search options may be available to help locate specific reports. Moderation features are available in Rocket.Chat version 6.2 and above.

output.summary: Retrieve information about a moderation report.
output.description: Fetches details about a specific moderation report, such as the reported message, reporter, and current status. This endpoint is useful for administrators or moderators who need to review the context and status of reported content in Rocket.Chat. The response typically includes information about the report, the user who submitted it, and any actions taken. Access to this endpoint may require appropriate permissions.

output.summary: Get detailed information about a specific moderation report.
output.description: Retrieve more details about a single moderation report by its reportId. This endpoint requires the 'view-moderation-console' permission and is useful for administrators or moderators who need to review the specifics of a reported message or user. The reportId must be provided as a query parameter.

output.summary: Dismiss moderation reports for a user or message.
output.description: Dismiss all moderation reports for a specific user by userId, or for a specific message by msgId. This endpoint requires the 'manage-moderation-actions' permission. Either userId or msgId must be provided in the request body. Use this to clear reports that have been reviewed or resolved.

output.summary: Dismiss one or more moderation reports.
output.description: Dismisses selected moderation reports for messages or users. This action deletes the reports but does not affect the reported messages or users themselves. Use this endpoint to clear reports after review when no further action is needed.

output.summary: Delete all reported messages for a user.
output.description: Deletes all messages reported for a specific user. This endpoint is typically used by moderators or administrators to remove all messages that have been flagged as reported for a given user. Proper permissions are required to perform this action, and it is important to ensure that the user ID is specified correctly to avoid unintended deletions.

output.summary: Delete all reported messages of a user.
output.description: Deletes all reports of messages belonging to the specified user. This endpoint requires the 'manage-moderation-actions' permission and a userId in the request body. It is intended for moderators or administrators to remove all reported messages associated with a user, helping to manage moderation actions efficiently. This action does not affect messages from other users.

output.summary: Retrieve all sessions of the authenticated user.
output.description: Retrieves all active sessions for the currently authenticated user, including details such as device type, browser, operating system, IP address, and login time. This endpoint is useful for users to monitor their active sessions and devices. Optional query parameters allow filtering, pagination, and sorting of the session list. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve all sessions for the authenticated user.
output.description: Retrieves all active sessions for the user making the request, including details such as device type, browser, operating system, IP address, and login time. This endpoint is useful for users to monitor their own active sessions and devices. Optional query parameters allow filtering, pagination, and sorting of the session list. Authentication is required.

output.summary: List all session parameters.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all session parameters available in the Rocket.Chat server. This endpoint is useful for administrators or integrations that need to inspect or manage session-related settings. Authentication may be required to access this endpoint, and the response typically includes details about each session parameter.

output.summary: Retrieve all user sessions in the workspace.
output.description: Retrieve the sessions of all users on the workspace. This endpoint requires two-factor authentication (2FA) and the 'view-device-management' permission. The response includes session details such as session ID, user information, device type, IP address, login time, and more. You can filter sessions using a regex, and paginate results with count, offset, and sort parameters. This endpoint is useful for administrators to monitor and manage device sessions across the workspace.

output.summary: Retrieve information about the current user's session.
output.description: This endpoint returns detailed information about the session owned by the authenticated user, including session ID, device details, IP address, login time, and user roles. It does not provide access to session information for other users. The sessionId query parameter is required to specify which session to retrieve information for.

output.summary: Retrieve information about the current user's session.
output.description: Retrieve detailed information about the session owned by the authenticated user, including session ID, device, IP address, login time, roles, and other session metadata. This endpoint only provides information about the user's own sessions and does not allow access to session data of other users.

output.summary: Retrieve session information for any user session as an admin.
output.description: This endpoint allows an authorized admin to retrieve detailed information about any session on the workspace, regardless of the session owner. It returns session details such as session ID, user information, device details, login time, and more. This endpoint requires 2FA and the 'view-device-management' permission. Use the 'sessionId' query parameter to specify which session to retrieve.

output.summary: Retrieve session information for any user session on the workspace.
output.description: Retrieve detailed information about any session on the workspace, regardless of the session owner. This endpoint allows authorized administrators to access session details for all users, including device, IP, login time, and user information. 2FA is required to use this endpoint. Permission required: 'view-device-management'.

output.summary: Log out the current user session.
output.description: Ends the current user's session by logging them out. This endpoint is typically used to terminate the authenticated user's session and invalidate their authentication token. No request body is required, and the user must be authenticated to use this endpoint.

output.summary: Log out the current user session.
output.description: Logs out the currently authenticated user by invalidating the session token associated with the request. This endpoint only affects the session corresponding to the provided authentication credentials and does not log out the user from other devices or sessions. Use this endpoint to securely end a session when the user chooses to log out.

output.summary: Log out the current user session.
output.description: Ends the current user session by invalidating the authentication token. This endpoint is typically used to log out a user from Rocket.Chat. The request may require the user's authentication token (x-Auth-Token) and user ID (x-User-Id) in the headers. After calling this endpoint, the user will need to log in again to obtain a new session token.

output.summary: Log out the current user session.
output.description: Ends the current user session by logging the user out. This endpoint invalidates the user's authentication token, requiring re-authentication for further API requests. It is typically used to securely terminate a session and ensure that the user's credentials are no longer valid for future requests.

output.summary: Get the current password policy for users.
output.description: Retrieves the current password policy settings for users in your Rocket.Chat workspace, including requirements such as minimum length, character types, and other password rules. Use this endpoint to programmatically check which password rules are enforced for user accounts. The pw.getPolicyReset endpoint has been removed as of version 7.0; use this endpoint instead. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Get the list of supported languages for auto-translation.
output.description: Retrieves the list of languages supported by the auto-translate feature. The language names in the response will be returned in the language specified by the required 'targetLanguage' query parameter (e.g., 'en' for English, 'es' for Spanish). Authentication is required. For more details on enabling and using auto-translate, see the Rocket.Chat Auto-Translate user guide.

output.summary: Save auto-translate settings for a room.
output.description: Saves auto-translate settings for a specific room. This endpoint allows you to enable or disable auto-translation, set the translation language, and specify the default language for a room. You must provide the room's ID, the setting field (such as 'autoTranslate' or 'autoTranslateLanguage'), and the value to apply. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Translate a message to a target language.
output.description: Auto-translates the provided message to the specified target language. Requires the message ID and the target language code. The response includes the translated message and related metadata. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve a list of configured email inboxes.
output.description: Gets the list of all email inboxes configured in the workspace. This endpoint requires the 'manage-email-inbox' permission. Supports pagination, sorting, and filtering using standard query parameters. The response includes details for each inbox, such as name, email address, status, department, and connection settings for SMTP and IMAP. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Set the email inbox for your server.
output.description: Sets the email inbox for your server, allowing you to configure incoming and outgoing email settings. Requires the 'manage-email-inbox' permission. You must provide the email address, name, active status, SMTP and IMAP credentials, and optionally a description, sender info, and department. This endpoint is used to add or update an email inbox configuration for handling emails within Rocket.Chat.

output.summary: Get details of an email inbox by ID.
output.description: Retrieves the details of a specific email inbox using its unique ID. Requires the 'manage-email-inbox' permission. The response includes information such as the inbox's name, email address, status, SMTP/IMAP configuration, department, and metadata. If the inbox is not found, a 'Resource not found' error is returned. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Delete an email inbox by ID.
output.description: Deletes an email inbox using its ID. This operation requires the 'manage-email-inbox' permission. If the specified email inbox does not exist, an error will be returned. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Search email inbox messages.
output.description: Searches for messages in the email inbox using specified query parameters. This endpoint allows filtering and searching through emails received in the Rocket.Chat email inbox integration. You can use various parameters to refine your search, such as keywords, sender, or date range. Results will include matching email messages and relevant metadata.

output.summary: Send a test email using a specific email inbox configuration.
output.description: Sends a test email using the email inbox configuration identified by the provided _id. This endpoint is useful for verifying that the email inbox settings are correct and that emails can be sent successfully. You must have the necessary permissions to use this endpoint, and the _id parameter should correspond to an existing email inbox configuration in your Rocket.Chat instance.

output.summary: Get a status shield SVG badge for your Rocket.Chat server.
output.description: Returns a dynamically generated SVG badge (shield) representing the status of your Rocket.Chat server. This endpoint is typically used for embedding a status badge in documentation, READMEs, or dashboards to visually indicate the server's health or availability. No authentication is required to access this endpoint. The badge can be customized with query parameters such as 'type' to display different status types (e.g., online, version).

output.summary: Search for users or rooms visible to the user.
output.description: Searches for users or rooms that are visible to the authenticated user. The endpoint only returns rooms that the user has not joined yet. The 'query' parameter is required and supports searching for channels using '#' and users using '@'. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve the last 1000 lines of server logs.
output.description: Retrieves the last 1000 lines of the Rocket.Chat server logs. This endpoint requires the 'view-logs' permission and returns log entries with their IDs, content, and timestamps. Useful for administrators to monitor or debug server activity. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Retrieve all registered licenses and their details in the workspace.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all registered licenses and their details in the workspace. This endpoint requires the 'view-privileged-setting' permission. It replaces the deprecated 'licenses.isEnterprise' and 'licenses.get' endpoints as of Rocket.Chat version 7.0. The response includes license information such as version, expiration, modules, limits, and other relevant details for license management.

output.summary: Add a license to the server.
output.description: Adds a new license to the Rocket.Chat server. This endpoint is typically used by administrators to upload or register a license key, which may be required to enable enterprise features or comply with licensing requirements. The request usually requires a valid license string in the request body and appropriate administrative permissions.

output.summary: Retrieve the maximum number of active users allowed by the license.
output.description: Returns the maximum number of active users permitted by the current workspace license, as well as the current number of active users. This endpoint requires authentication and is useful for administrators to monitor license limits and ensure compliance.

output.summary: Update the Jitsi video conference timeout for a room.
output.description: Updates the Jitsi video conference timeout for a specific room. This endpoint requires authentication and the roomId of the room whose Jitsi timeout should be updated. On success, it returns the new Jitsi timeout value.

output.summary: Get the specification of a slash command.
output.description: Retrieves the specification for a specific slash command by name, including its parameters, description, and whether it is client-only. Requires authentication. The 'command' query parameter must be provided with the name of the slash command you want to look up.

output.summary: List all available slash commands.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all available slash commands that can be used in Rocket.Chat. This endpoint returns details about each command, including its name and description, which can help users understand what commands are available and how to use them. No parameters are required. Useful for clients or integrations that want to display or utilize Rocket.Chat's slash command functionality.

output.summary: Get preview data for a slash command
output.description: Fetches preview data for a specified slash command in a given room. This endpoint is useful for commands that provide interactive previews or multiple options before execution, such as commands that require user selection. You must provide the command name and room ID, and you can optionally include parameters required by the command.

output.summary: Execute a preview item for a slash command.
output.description: Executes a selected preview item for a slash command in a specific room. This endpoint is used when a slash command provides a list of preview options (such as possible users, channels, or actions) and the user selects one to execute. The request must include the command name, room ID, thread ID (tmid), and the preview item object (with id, type, and value). Optionally, you can provide command parameters and a triggerId for UI interaction. This is typically used in interactive command workflows where the command requires user selection before final execution.

output.summary: Execute a slash command in a room.
output.description: Executes a specified slash command in the given room. You must provide the command name and the roomId. Optionally, you can include parameters (params), a thread ID (tmid), and a triggerId for UI interactions. This endpoint is useful for programmatically triggering any available slash command as if a user had typed it in the chat.

output.summary: Send emails to users in your workspace.
output.description: Send emails to users from your workspace. The request must include a valid 'from' email address and a subject. The body can include placeholders such as [unsubscribe], [name], [fname], [lname], and [email] for user personalization. If 'dryrun' is set to true, only one email will be sent to the 'from' address for testing. This endpoint requires authentication.

output.summary: Unsubscribe a user from mailer emails.
output.description: Unsubscribes a user from receiving mailer emails. Requires the user ID and the creation time of the mailer. This endpoint is typically used when a user clicks an unsubscribe link in an email sent from Rocket.Chat. The request body must include the user's ID (_id) and the createdAt timestamp of the mailer.

output.summary: Finds or creates an invite link for a room.
output.description: Creates a new invite link for a specified room or returns an existing one if it matches the given parameters. You must provide the room ID (rid), the number of days the invite should be valid (days, 0 for unlimited), and the maximum number of uses (maxUses, 0 for unlimited). Requires the 'create-invite-links' permission. The response includes details about the invite, such as its ID, expiration, and usage count.

output.summary: List all invites in the workspace.
output.description: Retrieves a list of all invite links created in the workspace, including their details such as expiration, usage limits, and associated rooms. Requires the 'create-invite-links' permission. This endpoint is useful for administrators to manage and review all active and expired invites.

output.summary: Delete an invite by ID.
output.description: Deletes an invite from the workspace using its ID. Requires the 'create-invite-links' permission. You must provide the invite ID to delete the corresponding invite. If the invite ID is invalid, an error will be returned.

output.summary: Report the usage of an invite token.
output.description: Report to the workspace that an invite token was used. This endpoint is typically called when a user joins a workspace or room using an invite link or token. The request body must include the 'token' field with the invite token value. On success, the response includes information about the room the invite was used for. Authentication is required.

output.summary: Validate an invite token.
output.description: Checks if an invite token is valid. This endpoint accepts a token in the request body and returns whether the token is valid or not. Useful for confirming the validity of an invite link before attempting to use it.

output.summary: Call a method with parameters using the DDP protocol.
output.description: Allows you to call a Rocket.Chat method by specifying the method name and parameters using the DDP (Distributed Data Protocol) over HTTP. This endpoint is typically used for advanced or custom integrations that require direct method calls, and the request body must include the parameters for the method being called. The response will contain the result of the method execution. Proper authentication is required, and the available methods and their parameters depend on your Rocket.Chat server version and configuration.

output.summary: Execute a Meteor method call.
output.description: Executes a specified Meteor (Realtime API) method call via a REST API request. Provide a JSON-encoded 'message' string in the request body that specifies the method name, parameters, and an id, following the Realtime API method call format. The response will contain the result of the method call as a JSON-encoded string. This endpoint is useful for clients that cannot use WebSockets and need to access Realtime API methods over HTTP. For details on the message format and available methods, refer to the Rocket.Chat Realtime API documentation.
